_comment: Everything the persona is allowed to say. One card per topic, written in first person so the model can restate it without rewording. Sources: src/constants.ts, the page copy, resume/resume.html and the READMEs of the public GitHub repositories. 'keywords' are extra search terms for retrieval only; they are never shown to the model. 'names' lists the proper names a visitor may use for the card's subject; a question that uses one is about documented work and must not be declined as out of scope. 'retrieval' holds the search settings shared by grounding.py and the site's chat.

cards.title: ft_transcendence (ShieldCore, bug bounty platform)
cards.text: ft_transcendence is what I am building now, with my team of five at 1337. Our platform is called ShieldCore: a multi-tenant bug bounty platform where organizations publish programs, researchers submit vulnerability reports and triagers validate them. It is still in progress. I am the product owner and I build the AI service. The stack of my part is Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Ollama and Docker.

cards.title: The AI service of ft_transcendence
cards.text: The AI service of ft_transcendence is my part of the platform: a FastAPI service that the backend calls. It detects duplicate vulnerability reports first, then it pre-triages a report and suggests a severity, and a RAG chatbot comes later. It is written in Python with FastAPI, Pydantic and async SQLAlchemy, and it runs in Docker. RAG and vector search pipelines in Python are my focus. I don't publish metrics for it.

cards.title: Duplicate report detection
cards.text: To find duplicate vulnerability reports, I embed each report with nomic-embed-text, which gives 768-dimension vectors, and I store them in pgvector with an HNSW cosine index. A new report is compared with the reports of the same program by vector search. I use HackerOne's disclosed reports dataset to seed and measure it. I don't publish metrics for it.
cards.keywords: duplicate duplicates detection detector deduplication vector search embeddings embedding model pgvector hnsw cosine index similarity nomic dataset hackerone database vectors precision recall accuracy

cards.title: Pre-triage and severity suggestions
cards.text: For pre-triage and severity I use llama3.2, running locally in Ollama. Pre-triage returns a scope check, a validity score, a suggested CWE, a summary and the missing information, as JSON validated with Pydantic. For severity, the model proposes a CVSS 3.1 vector and the score is computed with the cvss library, not by the model. It is a suggestion that a triager confirms. This part is in progress.

cards.title: ft_irc (IRC server)
cards.text: ft_irc is an IRC server I built in a team of three at 1337. It is written in C++98 and handles many connections in a single thread, with non-blocking sockets and a poll-based event loop. It works with standard IRC clients. It supports the commands PASS, NICK, USER, JOIN, PRIVMSG, KICK, INVITE, TOPIC and MODE. It is built with make and started with a port and a password: ./ircserv <port> <password>. The repository also has a bonus part, an IRC bot.

cards.title: Minishell
cards.text: Minishell is a small Bash-like shell in C, a team project at 1337. It supports pipes, redirections, heredocs, the && and || operators, subshells and wildcards, plus environment variable expansion. Its built-in commands are echo, cd, pwd, export, unset, env and exit. Inside, it has a lexer, a parser that builds an abstract syntax tree, an expander and an executor. It handles Ctrl-C, Ctrl-D and Ctrl-\.

cards.title: Philosophers
cards.text: Philosophers is my implementation of the dining philosophers problem in C with pthreads and mutexes, a 1337 project. It runs without deadlocks or starvation. Each philosopher is a thread and each fork is a mutex. Forks are taken in a defined order based on the philosopher's index, and a separate monitor thread checks whether a philosopher has died.

cards.text: miniRT is a ray tracer in C built on MiniLibX, a team project at 1337. It reads .rt scene files and renders spheres, planes and cylinders with ambient and point lighting and shadows. A scene file lists the ambient light, a camera, a point light and the objects.
